t:
In this division:
    (1) Congressional intelligence committees.—The term “congressional intelligence committees” means—
        (A) the Select Committee on Intelligence of the Senate; and 
        (B) the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence of the House of Representatives.  
    (2) Intelligence community.—The term “intelligence community” has the meaning given that term in section 3(4) of the National Security Act of 1947 (50 U.S.C. 3003(4)).

fable.w: This section only defines the terms "congressional intelligence committees" and "intelligence community" for the division. The tempting reading is that mentioning congressional committees implies consultation or reporting, but Congress is inside the federal government and no consultation process is created here in any case. No outside party such as states, the public, or experts is involved in any federal decision.

opus.w: This section only defines terms and does not set up any process for a federal decision. It might look relevant because it names congressional committees, which could later receive reports or briefings. But Congress and its committees are part of the federal government, and the section brings in no states, experts, or members of the public.

qwen_chat.w: This section only provides definitions for terms used in the statute. It does not require any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government. Both Congress and the intelligence community are considered inside the federal government, so any interaction between them would not constitute participation under the definition.
qwen_chat.s: In this division: (1) Congressional intelligence committees.—The term “congressional intelligence committees” means— (A) the Select Committee on Intelligence of the Senate; and (B) the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence of the House of Representatives. (2) Intelligence community.—The term “intelligence community” has the meaning given that term in section 3(4) of the National Security Act of 1947 (50 U.S.C. 3003(4)).
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that defining "intelligence community" or "congressional intelligence committees" implies some form of interaction or participation between these bodies. However, this section is purely definitional. It does not mandate any consultation, coordination, hearing, or advisory process involving outside parties. It simply establishes terminology for use elsewhere in the statute. Since there is no requirement for the federal government to consult with or coordinate with anyone outside the federal government (Congress and the intelligence community are both inside the federal government), this is not participation.
